messages:
maria: Hey team — customer (BigFin EU) asked for a full vendor risk packet for the POC. They need: data flow diagram, list of subprocessors, confirmation of where customer data rests (EU-only?), and whether we can sign SCCs / DPA. Can security/legal own the responses?

andrew: I can draft a redacted dataflow diagram. Quick note: hosted vs dedicated matters here — hosted may process in eu-west-1 but we have async telemetry that can land in us-central by default. Dedicated can be pinned to eu region and disable outbound telemetry.

andrew: diagram draft uploaded: s3://redwood-internal/diagrams/vendor-risk/1769801122-dataflow-v1.png (internal link)

kai: @maria thanks. Need to know if the POC will send raw PII or only hashed identifiers. Also will they request logs/backups access? That affects subprocessors list (e.g., backup provider).

maria: They'll send customer emails and transaction ids (PII) for enrichment. No log access requested by customer, but VR team wants to confirm retention & deletion flow.

jenna: We can execute SCCs and provide our standard DPA addendum. I'll run DPA review; need the customer's contact + any requested amendments. Template: https://confluence.internal/legal/dpa-template (internal).

andrew: Quick dataflow summary (for the packet):
```
Customer -> Redwood API (eu region) -> Load balancer -> Model serving (GPU pool, eu-west-1)
  - KV cache stored on local NVMe (ephemeral)
  - Short-term request logs -> S3 (eu-west-1) TTL=30d
  - Aggregated metrics -> Datadog (primary endpoint us-east-1) [optional, can be disabled]
  - Backups of model artifacts -> GCS (us-central) for multi-region redundancy (we can disable for dedicated/private)
```

andrew: Note: if customer requires EU-only subprocessors, recommend Dedicated or Private deployment. Hosted has third-party observability & cloud infra subprocessors.

kai: I will prepare: 1) redacted dataflow diagram, 2) canonical subprocessors CSV (names + country + purpose), 3) CAIQ matrix excerpt focused on data-in-transit/rest controls. ETA EOD tomorrow. Any specific controls they flagged?

maria: They flagged data residency, cross-border transfers, encryption at rest, and key management. Also asked whether we use customer-managed keys (CMK).

kai: We support CMKs via KMS integrations on Dedicated and Private; hosted supports envelope encryption with provider KMS (we can offer customer-managed in some enterprise deals). I'll include KMS notes in the packet.

ops-bot: DOCS_UPDATED: Updated diagram uploaded by andrew to s3://redwood-internal/diagrams/vendor-risk/1769801122-dataflow-v2.png :eyes:

jenna: For the subprocessors CSV I'll add legal notes about SCCs & subprocessors that require additional DPA clauses. Will ask procurement for current subprocessors registry if any vendors changed in last 30 days.

maria: Perfect — please cc me when you send to the customer's vendor risk contact (they want everything consolidated in one PDF). I'll coordinate the POC timeline once we have the packet.

kai: Will do. Also tagging @security for a quick sign-off before sending.

andrew: If you want a masked/high-level diagram for public-facing docs, I can produce a redacted SVG that removes internal hostnames. ETA 2pm today.

maria: Awesome — thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the customer's vendor risk rep and post their contact here.
